children: The number of oil and gas rigs actively drilling in the U.S. fell by 3 to 601 after rising by 1 a week ago, Baker Hughes reported Friday in its latest weekly survey.

The number of active drilling rigs targeting crude oil in the U.S. stayed flat at 463 in the week ended November 13, while gas rigs dropped 4 to 127 and rigs categorized as miscellaneous added 1 to 11.

The total rig count was up by 52, or 9.5%, compared to the same time last year, while the number of rigs drilling for oil rose by 46, or 11%, from a year ago, and gas rigs were up 2, or 1.6%, from a year earlier.
Rigs targeting oil in the Permian Basin gained 2 during the past week to 275, while the Eagle Ford and the Williston Basin remained unchanged at 43 and 30, respectively.

title: U.S. drilling rig count slips in latest Baker Hughes survey
